name: Tocopheryl acetate
description: Tocopheryl acetate (CAS 58-95-7 ), also known as Vitamin E acetate, is the esterified, shelf-stable form of Vitamin E used across food, pharmaceutical, and cosmetic manufacturing. Unlike free tocopherol, the acetate ester resists oxidation during processing and storage, making it the preferred supply form for formulators requiring consistent potency and long-term stability. It functions as both a nutritional supplement ingredient and an antioxidant stabilizer in finished products. In dietary supplements, it delivers Vitamin E activity in softgel capsules and fortified oils. Pharmaceutical manufacturers incorporate it into injectable formulations and oral dosage forms requiring a standardized, pharmacopeial-grade active. It is also used in vitamin blends for clinical applications. In personal care, it protects emulsions and skin-conditioning products from lipid oxidation. Food producers use it to fortify infant formula and cereal products to meet regulatory enrichment requirements. Tocopheryl acetate is supplied as a clear, viscous oil, with natural-source and synthetic versions available. Recognized specifications include USP , BP , Ph. Eur. , and food-grade FCC . Concentration variants such as 50% and 70% dilutions in carrier oils are also standard for premix and feed applications.
